answer: A stake-bonded identity registry resists Sybil attacks by making each identity costly to create: an agent locks a refundable deposit before it can earn, and the bond is slashed if peers prove it submitted duplicate or copied work. Like a saffron grower who plants one expensive bulb per thread of harvest, an attacker must pay real capital for every fake identity, while honest agents keep their stake. The shale of cheap throwaway accounts crumbles, because each new identity costs more than the rewards it can farm before detection.
